findings.title: Installer identity is not checked on first link
findings.body: The new GitHub-user check only runs after an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. If Integration.DoesNotExist, dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately and build_integration links that installation_id to the current Sentry org with no comparison to github_authenticated_user. GitHub fires the installation webhook and the browser redirect in parallel, so an attacker who knows a victim installation_id can finish this pipeline before the webhook creates the Integration, attach the victim's GitHub App install to the attacker's org, and then block the real installer via the "already installed on another organization" path. The OAuth step therefore does not enforce the mismatch failure described in the PR for the claim-on-create path.

findings.title: Reinstall crashes when metadata has no sender
findings.body: After an Integration exists with no OrganizationIntegration, the code always evaluates integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. build_integration only stores sender when pipeline state already has it, and this pipeline never binds sender, so installs created through the pipeline (and any older rows whose webhook payload did not write metadata.sender) have no sender. Re-attaching those installations raises KeyError instead of the integration error page, so a previously working reinstall 500s and never reaches next_step.

findings.title: User-mismatch test cannot tell a state failure from the new check
findings.body: test_github_user_mismatch (and the rewritten test_installation_not_found) only assert the generic "Invalid installation request." body. That same string is returned for a state/signature mismatch, a bad OAuth code, a missing login, and the sender comparison. The mismatch test also reuses the hardcoded state 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 after login_as(user_2) and a new org pipeline, so a state mismatch fails the request before GitHubInstallation ever compares logins. Nothing asserts that a matching installer is allowed, that a missing Integration is rejected, or that the 404 installation path still surfaces, so the security control can be bypassed or broken without these tests failing.
